assertion_results.evidence: The selected target was echoed near the top of the output.
A one-line casting summary described the panel mix.
One verdict line per panelist preceded the detailed panel section.
Five panel entries appeared in the entry shape the brief now carries inline.
Meta reported the number of agents requested.
Meta reported the number that returned.
Meta named the dispatch tool used.
The run reported dispatching five subagents before reading any result.
The target was named explicitly, so no confirmation question was asked.
Every dispatched panelist returned; nothing degraded.
git status in the fixture repository reported no changes after the run.
No commit was created; the fixture head remained the seed commit.
The fixture repository has no remote and no push was attempted.

evidence_note: Confirming observation for the inlined entry shape (revision a761017): the workaround reported at revision 2a96f3a — the orchestrator having to supply the panel-entry shape itself because the brief pointed at a section subagents never receive — did not recur, and entries came back in the briefed shape. The run's own panel then produced a finding that limits this very result: neither the skill's output shape nor this case's presence-only assertions can distinguish a real panel from a fabricated one, since an orchestrator that wrote the entries itself would emit the same fields and the same meta counts. This result is therefore evidence that the entry-shape fix works, and is not evidence that the panel was real. The strongest existing evidence for real dispatch remains the subagent-unavailable case, where refusing is only costly if the alternative — fabricating — was available.
